entries.proposition: Cohort: ten NICU infants, median 44.5 days at start, six preterm, indications lymphatic anomalies, haemangioma and one hemimegalencephaly.
entries.snippet: The indications were lymphatic malformation in four cases, generalized lymphatic anomaly in four cases, hemangioma in one case, and hemimegalencephaly in one case.

entries.proposition: Exposure: initial dose 0.02 mg/kg, adjusted to trough 5-15 ng/mL (a class-level observation; no recommendation follows).
entries.snippet: Sirolimus therapy was initiated at a dose of 0.02 mg/kg, and the dosage was subsequently adjusted based on trough levels to maintain a target concentration of 5–15 ng/mL.

entries.proposition: Thresholds are pragmatic, not validated for non-fasting NICU infants, and sampling was non-fasting.
entries.snippet: The definitions of dyslipidemia were based on previously published pediatric reference values [27, 28] and were used in this study as pragmatic classification thresholds rather than as diagnostic cutoffs specifically validated for non-fasting NICU neonates and infants

entries.proposition: After sirolimus all ten had triglycerides in the high range and nine of ten total cholesterol; two of ten had no baseline lipids.
entries.snippet: whereas after treatment all ten patients were classified as high.

entries.proposition: Severity: grade 2 triglycerides in four of ten, grade 3 in one, no grade 4 or 5; no pancreatitis or symptoms; no interruption or discontinuation for lipids.
entries.snippet: No clinically apparent pancreatitis or other clinically significant symptoms attributable to dyslipidemia were documented in the medical records.

entries.proposition: Reversibility rests on n = 5 and uses unscheduled labs, so time to normalisation was not estimated.
entries.snippet: lipid abnormalities improved in all cases

entries.proposition: The pharmacovigilance extract: 17,802 sirolimus reports, 430 dyslipidemia reports, 248 infant (28 d-23 mo) and 48 neonatal reports.
entries.snippet: A total of 17,802 sirolimus-related reports were retrieved from VigiBase up to 1 September 2025, including 430 dyslipidemia reports.

entries.proposition: The age-stratified models compare sirolimus reports with all other drugs in the database, not infants with adults on sirolimus.
entries.snippet: reports involving all other drugs in the database served as the exposure reference

entries.proposition: The Discussion reads the ratio of ratios as a "developmental window of vulnerability", which the authors elsewhere say cannot be read as incidence.
entries.snippet: The stark difference in aROR between infants and older children highlights a potential developmental window of vulnerability that closes as metabolic pathways mature.

entries.proposition: The authors declare that reporting odds ratios reflect reporting patterns, not true incidence or risk, and that dose and duration could not be included.
entries.snippet: the absence of denominator data means that disproportionality estimates and reporting odds ratios reflect reporting patterns rather than true incidence or risk

entries.proposition: Dose-dependence cannot be assessed: no weight, dose or duration in VigiBase; no concentration analysis in the cohort.
entries.snippet: Consequently, we cannot exclude the possibility that cumulative exposure or dose-dependent effects may have influenced the observed RORs.

entries.proposition: Time to onset in infants rests on four reports and is called a composite-report estimate.
entries.snippet: this estimate was based on only four infant reports and reflects the onset of composite dyslipidemia reports rather than fraction-specific laboratory changes

entries.proposition: The conclusion recommends lipid screening at baseline and within 7-14 days and calls current monitoring protocols likely inadequate; this is the authors recommendation, recorded as theirs and not adopted here.
entries.snippet: Current monitoring protocols derived from older populations are likely inadequate.

entries.proposition: Confounders named by the authors: parenteral nutrition, sepsis, indication, concomitant drugs, and the NICU context as a possible reason the neonate signal is lower.
entries.snippet: dyslipidemia might be attributed to total parenteral nutrition (TPN) or sepsis rather than the drug, leading to underreporting

entries.proposition: Table 2: the NA row carries N = 129, equal to the 45-64 year stratum N, and the Results text separately says 129 sirolimus reports had missing age; N (dyslipidemia reports) and report counts are different quantities that share the number.
entries.snippet: An additional 129 sirolimus-related reports had missing age information and were therefore not included in the age-stratified analyses.

entries.proposition: Table 2 caption: the stratum N column and the ROR columns that carry the infant 147.08 estimate.
entries.snippet: Crude reporting odds ratios (RORs) and adjusted reporting odds ratios (aRORs) for dyslipidemia associated with sirolimus exposure, estimated separately within each age stratum

entries.proposition: Fig 2 (300 ppi): forest plot of adjusted ROR on a log axis: neonates 20.15 [3.72-109.32], infants 147.08 [79.66-271.54], children 15.77, adolescents 4.89, adults 2.31 to 3.39; the infant interval does not overlap any other stratum. The numerators are 3, 19, 42, 16, 60, 129, 27 and 5 reports (Table 2); from the paper own counts the share of sirolimus reports that are dyslipidemia is 19 of 248 (7.7 percent) in infants, 42 of 872 (4.8 percent) in 2-11 year olds, 16 of 596 (2.7 percent) in 12-17 year olds, 3 of 48 (6.3 percent) in neonates (arithmetic by this reader from the text and Table 2).

entries.proposition: Fig 1 (300 ppi): individual trajectories for ten patients. Panels A,C,E (baseline available, 8 patients): TC rises above the 200 line in about five lines; TG in several lines returns to or below 100 mg/dL at later times (one near 75, one near 80 at about day 315-345) while others stay near 250; one TG spike near 545 mg/dL at about day 162. Panels B,D,F (no baseline, 2 patients): one patient starts at TC about 370 and falls to about 130 as the dose was halved; the other stays near 200.
